name: Anthony van Dyck
findings: Uses smoky black 2.3x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 1607 paintings here).
Uses raisin black 2.1x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 1607 paintings here).
Uses dark walnut 2.0x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 1607 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, courge green turns up as a small accent in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 2.9x the archive's rate (from 1607 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, yew green turns up as the lightest note in 62% of the paintings that hold it, 4.6x the archive's rate (from 1607 paintings here).
Pairs light grey with platinum more than chance would predict (3 of 1607 paintings here).
Pairs honey yellow with ochre brown more than chance would predict (5 of 1607 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, raisin black, black) covers 61% of his paintings here.
